disclaimer: Estimates only. Actual fines, costs and penalties vary by court and circumstances. Not legal advice.

AL.name: Alabama

default_limits.basis: Ala. Code 32-5A-171: 30 urban district; 35 unpaved; 45 county-paved roads in unincorporated areas; 55 other; 65 on 4+ lane highways; 70 interstate.

fine.notes: Uniform fine schedule (Ala. R. Jud. Admin. 20) from a 2025 city copy; court costs are added and are most of the total. Construction zone: $250. Max $100 first offense (32-5A-8).

court_costs.notes: Vary by court; not found.

points.notes: ALEA. 12 pts in 2 yrs = 60-day suspension. Reckless driving = 6.

zones.work_zone: $250 fine on uniform schedule.
zones.school_zone: Not verified.

court.reason: 26+ over: 5 points; higher schedule fine from 25+.

arrest.offense: Reckless driving (misdemeanor); no speed threshold
arrest.license: Up to 6 months suspension possible; 6 points

trucks.notes: Placarded hazmat/explosives/flammables: 55 max (32-5A-171(5)).

AL.notes: 65 applies on 4+ lane highways only; trunk/primary set to 55 since lane count unknown. unclassified=45 assumes county-paved rural road (35 if unpaved). ALEA lists 25 for residential; statute says 30 urban district. 32-5A-8 ($100/10 days) and reckless penalties read only from a secondary slide deck. HB638 (2026) would extend city enforcement to police jurisdiction (eff. Oct 1, 2026 if passed; status unknown).

AK.name: Alaska

default_limits.basis: 13 AAC 02.275(b): 15 alleys, 20 business districts, 25 residence districts, 55 other roadways. Higher limits (e.g. 65) only where posted under 13 AAC 02.280. OSM mapping approximate; use 20 in business districts, 15 in alleys.

fine.notes: Statewide bail schedule (Admin. R. 43.1): $8/mph for 3-19 over, $12/mph for 20+ over (e.g. 3 over = $24). Capped at $300 (AS 28.90.010(c)). Municipal ordinances may differ.

court_costs.notes: State surcharge (AS 12.55.039): $20 when fine is $30+ (so none on a $24 ticket). Mandatory, not waivable.

points.notes: School zone speeding 6 pts; reckless driving 10 pts. Suspension at 12 pts in 12 mo or 18 in 24 mo (threshold from secondary source).

zones.work_zone: Fine doubled in highway work zones; max $600.
zones.school_zone: Marked school/playground zones: $12/mph (3-9 over), $14/mph (10-19), $16/mph (20+); 6 pts.

court.reason: Rate jumps from $8 to $12 per mph and points from 4 to 6. Still a payable infraction (no mandatory court).

arrest.offense: Reckless driving (misdemeanor) - no speed number; requires substantial, unjustifiable risk that is a gross deviation from reasonable driving
arrest.license: first offense: revocation, 30 days minimum (secondary source)

trucks.notes: No separate car/truck limits found in 13 AAC 02.275. Commercial-vehicle speeding under 13 AAC 03 has higher bail ($12-$20/mph). Not fully verified.

sources.title: Alaska Court System PUB-132 Vehicle & Traffic Offenses Booklet (Oct 2026)
Alaska Admin. Rule 43.1 bail schedule (courtrules.net mirror)

AK.notes: Fines/points from official court booklet (high). Reckless driving max fine not verified from official text (secondary source says $1,000) - left null. akleg.gov and courts.alaska.gov rule text were not reachable; statutes read via mirrors. Anchorage and other cities use their own ordinances and fine schedules.

AZ.name: Arizona

default_limits.basis: A.R.S. § 28-701(B) prima facie limits: 15 approaching a school crossing, 25 in business/residential districts, 65 in other locations. 75 on interstates only where posted.

fine.notes: Civil traffic violation; court sets fine up to $250 plus surcharges (§ 28-1598). Up to 10 over in qualifying zones = 'waste of a finite resource': $15 + surcharges (§ 28-702.01). Typical amounts not verified.

court_costs.notes: State surcharges added on top of the fine; amounts not verified from an official source.

points.notes: 3 points (secondary sources). Waste-of-finite-resource tickets (up to 10 over) are not reported and carry no points. 8 pts/12 mo = traffic school; 13+ = suspension.

zones.school_zone: 15 mph prima facie approaching a school crossing (§ 28-701); over 35 there is a criminal misdemeanor (§ 28-701.02).

court.reason: Over 10 mph is no longer a 'waste of finite resource' ticket: full fine, reported to MVD, 3 points.

arrest.offense: Excessive speed / criminal speeding (class 3 misdemeanor)
arrest.license: 3 points; no automatic suspension
arrest.reason: § 28-701.02: criminal at 21+ over posted limit anywhere (no 85 mph rule in current text); also over 45 on an unposted business/residential street, or over 35 approaching a school crossing (not expressible as min_over/min_speed).

trucks.notes: No truck-specific statewide limit found in the text reviewed; obey posted truck limits.

sources.title: AZ HB2059 (57th Leg. 2nd Reg., prefiled 12/15/2025) - shows current § 28-701.02 and § 28-702.01 text
AZ HB2409 (57th Leg. 1st Reg., 2025) - shows § 28-701.02 base text
AZ HB2366 (2021) - shows older 85 mph text
Salwin Law - criminal speed (secondary: 30 days, $500, 3 points)
AZ Court Help - civil traffic fines ($250 + surcharges)

AZ.notes: Arrest threshold confirmed from azleg.gov § 28-701.02: more than 20 over anywhere; no 85 mph text (older law-firm pages are outdated). Class 3 misdemeanor = 30 days (§ 13-707); $500 fine not checked against § 13-802. Points (3) not verified from AAC R17-4-404 table.

AR.name: Arkansas

default_limits.basis: Ark. Code 27-51-201 (2020 text read): 30 in any urban district; 65 urban controlled-access highways; 75 max rural 4+ lane divided controlled-access (ArDOT posts; 70 for CMVs). Text read sets no numeric default for cars on other rural roads, only 'reasonable and prudent' (27-51-201(a)); 50 for trucks 1.5 ton+.

fine.notes: Speeding is a misdemeanor. 1st offense in a year: up to $100 and/or 10 days; 2nd up to $200/20 days; 3rd up to $500/6 mo (per secondary sources; statute text not read). No statewide fine schedule found.

court_costs.notes: Uniform costs set by Ark. Code 16-10-305, plus local fees; amount not verified.

points.notes: DFA schedule (Reg. 1993-9). Reckless = 8 pts. 10 pts = warning; 14+ = hearing, possible suspension (3 mo to 1 yr).

zones.work_zone: Fines reportedly doubled in construction zones (secondary source only; statute not verified).
zones.school_zone: 25 mph school-zone limit per secondary source; penalty not verified.

court.reason: Excessive speeding: Class C misdemeanor, higher fine and jail exposure.

arrest.offense: Excessive speeding, more than 15 mph over posted limit (Class C misdemeanor)
arrest.license: Court may suspend for moving violations (secondary source); 8 pts if 31+ over

trucks.notes: Trucks 1.5 ton+: 50 off controlled-access roads; CMVs (26,001 lb+) 70 on rural 75-mph freeways (27-51-201).

sources.title: Ark. Reg. 1993-9 Driver Services (points) - Cornell LII
ASMSA Vehicle Safety Program (reproduces DFA points table)
Ark. Admin. of Justice Fund rule (16-10-305 ref) - Cornell LII

AR.notes: Official AR code site not reachable; statute text via Justia/FindLaw mirrors (2020/2024) and secondary sites. 'In excess of 15 over' = 16+. Any AR speeding is technically a misdemeanor (up to 10 days jail 1st offense). Reckless driving (27-50-308, Class B, 5-90 days, $25-500) has no speed number. 27-50-306: extra $5 if 20+ over with a minor aboard. Rural car default limit unverified - recheck current 27-51-201.

CA.name: California

default_limits.basis: Veh. Code § 22349(a) 65 max on highways; § 22349(b) 55 on two-lane undivided highways unless posted higher; § 22352 25 in business/residence districts, 15 in alleys. 70 only where posted (§ 22356). Trunk=65 assumes multi-lane/divided; a two-lane undivided trunk is 55.

fine.notes: Base fines are only $35/$70/$100; state & county penalty assessments roughly 4.5x them. Amounts shown are Santa Clara 2025 total bail (varies a few dollars by county; other counties list ~$238/$367/$490 incl. fees). max_fine = $100 statutory base (VC 42001); over 100 mph base up to $500.

court_costs.notes: $40 court operations (PC 1465.8) + $35 conviction assessment (GC 70373) per conviction, on top of total bail. Traffic school adds a $49 fee.

points.notes: 1 point for speeding (VC 12810(f)); 2 points if over 100 mph (VC 12810(d), § 22348(b)) or reckless driving. Traffic school can mask 1 point.

zones.work_zone: Highway construction zone fines doubled base (VC 42009): total bail $287 / $445 / $568 (Santa Clara 2025).
zones.school_zone: 25 mph prima facie near schools when children present and posted (VC 22352); cities may adopt 20 mph school zones (2026 change).

court.reason: 26+ over is the top fine bracket; over 100 mph (VC 22348(b)) raises the base fine cap to $500, 2 points, and court may suspend license up to 30 days.

arrest.offense: Reckless driving (VC 23103) - no speed threshold; requires willful or wanton disregard for safety
arrest.license: 2 points; no automatic suspension for first offense

trucks.notes: 55 mph max on all highways for trucks with 3+ axles, any truck or passenger vehicle towing a trailer, school buses with pupils, farm labor vehicles, explosives haulers (VC 22406). They must use the right lane (VC 22348(c)) and cannot use 70 mph zones.

sources.title: Santa Clara Superior Court 2025 Traffic Bail Schedule (speed chart, fees)
San Luis Obispo Superior Court speed chart ($238/$367/$490 totals, 2017)
Crescenta Valley Weekly - Speed Law Changes in 2026 (secondary)

CA.notes: Statutes high confidence (read via california.public.law mirror; leginfo.ca.gov blocked). Fine totals from Santa Clara 2025 county schedule; could not extract the statewide 2026 UBPS speed chart page, but base fines unchanged since 2017. No criminal speed threshold: even 100+ mph is an infraction. Speed cameras (AB 645 pilot cities) use separate civil fines $50-$500.

CO.name: Colorado

default_limits.basis: C.R.S. 42-4-1101(2): 20 narrow winding mountain roads/blind curves; 25 business district; 30 residence district; 40 open mountain highways; 55 other open highways; 65 surfaced 4-lane interstates and freeways/expressways (trunk expressways may be 65). Absolute max 75 (8)(b).

fine.notes: State penalty-assessment schedule (42-4-1701(4)). 25+ over is a misdemeanor: no ticket fine, court sets $150-$300. Max shown is top of schedule; municipal courts use own schedules.

court_costs.notes: Paying the ticket: surcharge added to fine ($6/$10/$16/$32 by bracket). If convicted in county court: ~$24 docket fee (JDF 1, 2023). Municipal courts vary.

points.notes: C.R.S. 42-2-127(5)(f). Adults suspended at 12 pts in 12 months or 18 in 24; 40+ over alone reaches 12.

zones.work_zone: Fine and surcharge doubled in designated work zones; 25+ over there is a class 1 misdemeanor (up to 1 yr, $1,000).
zones.school_zone: Fine and surcharge doubled in school zones (42-4-1701(4)(d)). Wildlife crossing zones also doubled.

court.reason: 25+ over (or 25+ over the 75 max) is a misdemeanor: no pay-by-mail, must appear in court.

arrest.offense: Speeding 25+ mph over (class 2 misdemeanor traffic offense)
arrest.license: 6 points (25-39 over) or 12 points (40+ over, triggers suspension for adults)

trucks.notes: Only narrow case: trash trucks (single rear axle, over 20,000 lb) 45 mph where higher is posted (42-4-1101(2)(e)). Commercial vehicle speeding on steep-grade zones is doubled.

sources.title: Colorado Legislative Council: Penalties for speeding violations
Colorado Judicial JDF 1 court filing fees and costs

CO.notes: Statute text read via public.law (2024 C.R.S., current through fall 2025), not leg.colorado.gov directly. Limits are prima facie (except 75 max). Misdemeanor minimum is 10 days jail or $150 fine. 2026 bills on speed cameras not reflected.

CT.name: Connecticut

default_limits.basis: Not verified. The text of CGS 14-219 couldn't be retrieved. Limits are set by the state traffic authority or local traffic authorities and posted. GHSA lists max 65 for rural interstates and 55 for urban interstates. OLR (1994) described 14-219(a) as barring speeds over 55 statewide; 65 on suitable multilane limited-access highways since PA 98-181. Not confirmed against current text, so left null.

fine.notes: Totals including fees, from a secondary source. Higher by actual speed: 71-75 mph $228, 76-80 $269, 81-85 $309. Above 85 mph is reckless driving.

court_costs.notes: Included in the amounts above. The official breakdown wasn't found.

points.notes: 1 point for any speeding (Regs. 14-137a-5). About 10 points in 24 months brings a 30+ day suspension.

zones.work_zone: Higher fines (secondary source: about $50-$90 more).
zones.school_zone: Higher fines (secondary source: about $50-$90 more).

court.reason: Above 85 mph is reckless driving, a criminal charge that must be handled in court.

arrest.offense: Reckless driving (over 85 mph is a violation per se). Above 100 mph: enhanced penalty, PA 25-19.

trucks.notes: Not verified.

CT.notes: The arrest tier is solid: above 85 mph is reckless driving, first offense $100-$300 and/or 30 days. Above 100 mph: $200-$600 and/or 30 days. No defaults and no official fine schedule were verified; fines are from a secondary source. Speeding suspension starts at the 4th offense; OLR says points may not be assessed on mail-in payment.

DE.name: Delaware

default_limits.basis: 21 Del. C. § 4169(a): 25 business district; 20 or 25 residence district (road owner's choice); 50 two-lane roads; 55 four-lane or divided. Mapping assumes motorway/trunk divided, others two-lane. 65 only where posted (e.g. SR 1).

fine.notes: Fine = $20 + rate x every mph over (§ 4169(c)), e.g. 10 over = $30, 20 over = $80. Repeat within 24 mo: $25 + $2/$3/$4 per mph. No cap stated. Plus court costs and assessments.

court_costs.notes: Costs and assessments added on top of fine; amounts not found in a readable official source. Varies by court (JP vs. alderman).

points.notes: DMV Reg. 2208. No points if 1-14 over, paid by voluntary assessment, and no speeding conviction in 3 yrs (JP Court). 12 pts in 24 mo = course or 2-mo suspension; 14 = 4-mo suspension.

zones.work_zone: Extra assessments apply in work zones (§ 4170A(g)); amounts not verified.
zones.school_zone: 20 mph where posted with times/conditions (§ 4169(a)); fine schedule same formula.

court.reason: 25+ over: mandatory 1-month license suspension, +1 month per extra 5 mph (course option at 25-29 over). 90+ mph is a separate reckless-driving offense.

arrest.offense: Driving 90 mph or more (reckless driving statute, § 4175(b))
arrest.license: No suspension stated in § 4175(b); 25+ over triggers DMV suspension separately

trucks.notes: No truck-specific limits in § 4169; DelDOT may set limits by vehicle type (§ 4169(b)).

sources.title: 21 Del. C. ch. 41 subch. IX (§ 4175 reckless)

DE.notes: Only speed-number criminal tier is 90+ mph (§ 4175(b), since 2023): fine $150-300 and/or safety course, no jail for 1st. General reckless driving (§ 4175(c), no mph number) = $100-300 and/or 10-30 days. JP Court says most traffic offenses are handled as criminal. Court costs unverified.

DC.name: District of Columbia

default_limits.basis: DDOT: 20 mph on any street/highway with no posted limit (since June 1, 2020); alleys 15. Arterials/freeways are normally posted higher.

fine.notes: MPD collateral book (Jan 2025). 'Over 25' is $400 on controlled-access roads, $500 elsewhere. Camera fines same amounts, no points.

court_costs.notes: Civil infraction handled by DC DMV; no separate court cost found.

points.notes: Reckless 6 pts; aggravated reckless 12 pts + revocation. 1-10 over not on DMV chart (0 pts).

zones.work_zone: Fines doubled in work zones (DDOT).
zones.school_zone: 15 mph by schools at posted times/arrival-dismissal; fines doubled (DDOT).

court.reason: 20+ over is criminal reckless driving.

arrest.offense: Reckless driving (criminal)
arrest.license: 6 points; 30+ over = aggravated reckless: up to 180 days, 12 pts, revocation

trucks.notes: No separate truck default found.

DC.notes: Reckless threshold is 20+ over (STEER Act era amendments); 30+ over is aggravated reckless. Reckless max fine $500 read from a WomensLaw copy of § 22-3571.01; one law firm says $1,000 - verify. 18 DCMR fine schedule itself not read.

FL.name: Florida

default_limits.basis: Fla. Stat. 316.183(2): 30 in business/residence districts, 55 at all other locations. Higher limits (up to 70 on limited-access) only where set and posted under 316.187.

fine.notes: Base civil penalty, 318.18(3)(b); 1-5 over = warning. Up to $500 if contested at hearing (318.14(5)). 30+ over doubled on 2nd within 12 months.

court_costs.notes: Varies by county; statewide + local add-ons. Observed add-on over base fine: Lake $106, Miami-Dade $119 (e.g. 10-14 over totals $206/$219).

points.notes: 322.27(3)(d): 6 pts if speeding causes a crash. 12 pts/12 mo = up to 30-day suspension.

zones.work_zone: Fine doubled when construction workers present (318.18(3)(e)).
zones.school_zone: Fine doubled; $50 for up to 5 over (318.18(3)(c)).

court.reason: Mandatory court hearing for 30+ over (318.19(5), as amended by 2025 HB 351); no pay-by-mail.

arrest.offense: Dangerous excessive speeding (criminal; Fla. Stat. 316.1922)
arrest.license: None for 1st conviction; 2nd within 5 yrs = 180-day to 1-yr revocation

trucks.notes: No truck-specific limit found in 316.183; not exhaustively checked.

FL.notes: 316.1922 at 100+ mph also requires driving that threatens people/property or interferes with traffic; 50+ over alone suffices. Reckless driving (316.192, up to 90 days) has no speed number. Senate bill summary said mandatory hearing at 50+, but enrolled bill and 2025 statute text say 30+; used 30. Points for 316.1922 not stated in 322.27.

GA.name: Georgia

default_limits.basis: O.C.G.A. 40-6-181(b): 30 urban/residential district; 35 unpaved county road; 55 other locations. 70 interstate / 65 divided highways apply only when posted.

fine.notes: Brackets are statutory MAXIMUM first-offense fines (40-6-1(b)); courts set actual amounts. 34+ over has no special cap, so general misdemeanor max $1,000 applies (17-10-3). Surcharges extra.

court_costs.notes: Varies by court; state surcharges added on top of fine. No statewide figure found.

points.notes: 15 points in 24 months = suspension (DDS).

zones.work_zone: Same point scale applies (40-6-188); fine amounts not verified.
zones.school_zone: Not verified.

court.reason: 34+ over: no fine cap (up to $1,000/12 mo), 6 points. 85+ mph (or 75+ on two-lane road): $200 Super Speeder state fee, license suspended if unpaid.

arrest.offense: Reckless driving (misdemeanor); no speed threshold
arrest.license: 4 points

trucks.notes: No truck-specific limit in 40-6-181 text reviewed.

GA.notes: All GA speeding is a misdemeanor (40-6-1(a)), so custodial arrest is legally possible at any speed; no statutory 'criminal speed' number. 40-6-181 read from law-firm copy; reckless text from 2006 version. Super Speeder fee is owed to DDS, not the court.

HI.name: Hawaii

default_limits.basis: No statewide statutory default found. HRS 291C-102 enforces limits set by county ordinance or by official signs (state DOT on state highways). Use posted/OSM maxspeed only.

fine.notes: Max $200 first offense (HRS 291C-161). Court bail schedule not found online. Typical range is from 2025 HDOT speed-camera citations ($167-$317, rising with mph over).

court_costs.notes: $7 driver education assessment on every moving violation (HRS 286G-3), plus $10 neurotrauma surcharge if more than 10 over (HRS 291C-102(b)).

points.notes: No points system. Violations tracked on a traffic abstract (2026 House Res. 88 urged DOT to consider points).

zones.work_zone: Higher fine in construction zones (HRS 291C-104); secondary source says $250 + $100 surcharge. Not verified officially.
zones.school_zone: Higher fine in school zones (HRS 291C-104); secondary source says $250 + surcharge. Not verified officially.

court.reason: Over 10 mph adds $10 surcharge; HDOT cameras target 11+ over. Still a payable infraction.

arrest.offense: Excessive speeding (petty misdemeanor); 3rd within 5 years is a misdemeanor
arrest.license: 30-day suspension (or 15 days + 15 days work-only restricted)

trucks.notes: No statewide truck-specific limits found; limits are set by sign/ordinance. Not verified.

sources.title: HB54 HD2 (2026) excessive speeding bill text (current-law penalties)
HR 88 HD1 (2026) - traffic abstract, no points

HI.notes: Excessive speeding (30+ over or 80+ mph) is criminal: first offense $500-$1,000 fine, 36 hrs community service or 48 hrs-5 days jail, 30-day suspension, plus $75 driver ed assessment, $25 neurotrauma, up to $100 trauma surcharge (Act 170, 2025). Ordinary fine schedule and zone fines not verified from official source.

ID.name: Idaho

default_limits.basis: I.C. 49-654(2)(a): 35 residential/business/urban districts, 75 interstates, 65 state highways, 55 other locations. Interstates may be raised to 80 and state highways to 70 by study. OSM mapping approximate.

fine.notes: Statewide fixed schedule (Idaho Infraction Rule 9(b), eff. 7/1/2025). With court costs: $90 (1-15 over), $155 (16+ over). Statutory max for the infraction not verified.

court_costs.notes: Fixed statewide: tech $10, county $5, POST $15, surcharge $10, general $16.50.

points.notes: Work zone speeding 4 pts, school zone 3 pts. Suspension: 12 pts/12 mo = 30 days, 18/24 mo = 90 days, 24/36 mo = 6 months (IDAPA 39.02.71).

zones.work_zone: Fine $50 + $56.50 costs = $106.50 (I.C. 49-657). Over 20 mph over in an active construction zone with workers present and visible = reckless driving (misdemeanor), since 7/1/2026.
zones.school_zone: Fine $100 + $56.50 costs = $156.50 (I.C. 49-658). Over 20 mph over in an active school zone with children present and visible = reckless driving, since 7/1/2026.

court.reason: Fine jumps from $90 to $155 total and points from 3 to 4. Still a payable infraction.

arrest.offense: Reckless driving (misdemeanor) - no speed number on ordinary roads; requires careless/heedless driving endangering others
arrest.license: no mandatory suspension on first conviction; mandatory on repeat within 5 years

trucks.notes: Since 7/1/2026 (HB 664), trucks with 5+ axles over 26,000 lb have the same limits as cars (up to 80 on posted interstates). Before that, heavy trucks were capped lower.

ID.notes: Passing allowance: cars/pickups not towing may go up to 15 over to pass on 2-lane roads posted 55+ (49-654(2)(b)); fines then figured from limit+15. Penalty schedule effective 7/1/2025; check for FY2027 update. Infraction max fine not confirmed.

IL.name: Illinois

default_limits.basis: 625 ILCS 5/11-601: 30 in urban districts, 15 in alleys, 70 on interstates outside urban districts, 65 only on 4-lane divided highways designated by IDOT (posted), 55 all other roads

fine.notes: 1-25 over is a petty offense: pay-by-mail guilty plea is a flat $164 (Schedule 12, all-in). In court: fine ($25 min, $1,000 max) plus $226 assessment. 26+ over is a misdemeanor, court decides.

court_costs.notes: Included in the $164 mail-in amount. If convicted in court, Schedule 10 assessment is $226 (+ up to $28 in Cook County).

points.notes: Secretary of State point values (92 Ill. Adm. Code 1040.20). Court supervision is not a conviction and adds no points.

zones.work_zone: Min $250 fine first offense (workers present or not, if posted)
zones.school_zone: 20 mph on school days 6:30am-4pm when children present; min $150 fine first offense; 26+ over = aggravated (55 points)

court.reason: Becomes a criminal misdemeanor; 50 points; mail-in $164 plea covers only minor (petty) traffic offenses

arrest.offense: Speeding 26+ over (Class B misdemeanor); 35+ over is Class A
arrest.license: 50 points per conviction

trucks.notes: Vehicles 8,001 lb+ in Cook, DuPage, Kane, Lake, McHenry, Will counties: 60 on interstates, 55 elsewhere

sources.title: 730 ILCS 5/5-4.5-60 (Class B sentence) - law firm reproduction of statute
Ill. S. Ct. Rule 529 (written plea, Schedule 12)
Rock Island County traffic financial sentencing order

IL.notes: Statutory limits, misdemeanor thresholds and points verified from ilga.gov. Work-zone $250 read from P.A. 99-212 (2015 text), not the current compiled section. Class B misdemeanor max read from a law-firm copy of the statute. Residential=30 assumes urban district; rural unposted roads are 55.

IN.name: Indiana

default_limits.basis: IC 9-21-5-2 (2025, am. P.L.173-2025): 30 urban district, 55 general, 70 interstates outside urbanized areas 50k+, 60 rural 4-lane divided, 65 I-465 and INDOT freeways, 15 alleys

fine.notes: Class C infraction; judge sets amount, max $500 (IC 34-28-5-4). Typical $100-$200 total incl. costs (secondary source).

court_costs.notes: Statutory infraction costs/fees ~$132-$135 (SBOA, IC 33-37); typical_range already includes them.

points.notes: 140 IAC 1-4.5. Points last 2 yrs; 2+ offenses in 12 months can require a Driver Safety Program.

zones.work_zone: Higher fines in construction zones; amounts not verified.
zones.school_zone: Not verified.

court.reason: 6 points (top bracket).

arrest.offense: Reckless driving (Class C misdemeanor) - 'unreasonably high speed' endangering others, no speed number

trucks.notes: Over 26,000 lb (not buses): 65 on rural interstates and toll road (IC 9-21-5-2).

sources.title: Reckless driving penalties (secondary, law info site)
Felony speeding in Indiana (secondary, law firm)
Indiana SBOA court costs and fees by case type (2020)
IC 34-28-5-4 infraction judgments (2006 Justia; Class C max $500)
IC 35-50-3-4 Class C misdemeanor (2006 Justia; 60 days/$500)

IN.notes: Limits, points, infraction max ($500), costs and Class C misdemeanor penalty (60 days/$500) checked against official/statutory text. Reckless driving being a Class C misdemeanor (IC 9-21-8-52) is from secondary sources only. No speed-based criminal threshold. Interstates in urbanized areas are 65.

IA.name: Iowa

default_limits.basis: Iowa Code § 321.285: 55 default; 70 interstates; 65 divided multilane controlled-access/selected divided highways; 25 residence/school districts; 20 business districts; 45 suburban districts; 35 state parks; unpaved secondary roads 55 day/50 night.

fine.notes: Scheduled fines, Iowa Code § 805.8A(5)(a). Over 20: $135 + $5 per mph above 20 (= $35 + $5 x mph over; 21 over = $140, 30 over = $185). No cap in schedule.

court_costs.notes: $55 court costs (§ 602.8106) plus 15% crime services surcharge on the fine. E.g. 6-10 over: $55 + $8.25 + $55 = $118.25.

points.notes: No points. 3+ moving violations in 12 months can suspend license. First two tickets in 12 months for 10 or less over in a 35-55 zone are not counted.

zones.school_zone: 25 mph school district limit (§ 321.285); no separate fine verified.

court.reason: 25+ over is a 'serious violation': license may be suspended (25-29 over may get Driver Improvement Program instead).

arrest.offense: Reckless driving (§ 321.277), simple misdemeanor; no speed number in statute
arrest.license: Speeding 25+ over: possible DOT suspension (§ 321.210)

trucks.notes: No separate truck limit found in § 321.285 summary.

sources.title: Iowa SF 378 (91st GA) - explanation summarizing § 321.285 limits
Iowa DPS Compendium of Scheduled Violations (July 2023)

IA.notes: All speeding is technically a simple misdemeanor, but scheduled (mail-in). No speed makes it reckless by itself; reckless driving text (§ 321.277) not read directly. Limits taken from a 2025 bill's summary of § 321.285, not the code text. 2026 code not fetched; 2023 code used for costs/penalty.

KS.name: Kansas

default_limits.basis: K.S.A. 8-1558(a): 30 urban district, 75 posted separated multilane highways, 55 county/township highways, 65 all other highways. Mapping assumes tertiary/unclassified = county roads.

fine.notes: K.S.A. 8-2118 statewide schedule: $45 (1-10 over); $45 + $6/mph beyond 10; $105 + $9/mph beyond 20; $195 + $15/mph beyond 30. Doubled in school and road-construction zones. Court costs extra.

court_costs.notes: Not verified. A secondary source says about $25; treat as unreliable.

points.notes: No points. 3+ moving violations in 12 months can lead to suspension (K.S.A. 8-255, per secondary source).

zones.work_zone: Fine doubled in road construction zones (K.S.A. 8-2118(e)).

LA.name: Louisiana

MA.name: Massachusetts

MN.name: Minnesota

default_limits.basis: Minn. Stat. § 169.14 subd. 2: 30 urban district; 55 elsewhere; 65 noninterstate expressways/freeways; 70 rural interstate, 65 interstate in urbanized areas; 10 in alleys; 25 residential roadway / 35 rural residential district only if adopted by road authority.

ND.name: North Dakota

default_limits.basis: NDCC 39-09-02(1) as amended by HB 1298 (2025): 25 business/residence districts and parks, 55 gravel/loose-surface roads and unposted paved two-lane county/township roads, 65 paved two-lane highways if posted, 70 divided multilane, 80 interstates (since 8/1/2025). OSM mapping approximate; 65 applies only where posted.

fine.notes: Roads posted 65 or less: $3/mph over, $20 minimum, +$20 at 16+ over (30+ over row computes $20 + $3/mph; HP report examples: 42 over = $146). Roads posted over 65: $5/mph, $20 minimum, +$20 at 16+ over. Set by statute (NDCC 39-06.1-06, HB 1298, eff. 8/1/2025). Cities may set own fees.

court_costs.notes: Statutory fee only; Highway Patrol says no court administration fee is added to a noncriminal traffic citation. Costs may apply if contested.

points.notes: Zones 65 or less. Over 65: 1-5 0, 6-10 1, 11-15 3, 16-20 5, 21-25 7, 26-30 10, 31-35 12, 36+ 15. 12+ points = 7-day suspension per point over 11. Under 18: canceled at 6.

zones.work_zone: Higher fee when workers present and sign says minimum fee. Was $80 + $2/mph over 10; news reports HB 1298 raised it to $150 (not confirmed from enrolled text).
zones.school_zone: 20 mph when children present. $40 for 1-10 over, +$1/mph beyond 10 (or the regular fee if greater).

court.reason: At 16+ over, +$20 fee and 3+ points (5+ on 65+ roads). Still a noncriminal payable fee.

arrest.offense: Reckless driving (class B misdemeanor) - no speed number in statute; officer discretion (e.g. arrests at 119 mph)
arrest.license: 8 points (aggravated reckless with injury: class A, 12 points)

trucks.notes: No separate truck speed limits found in 39-09-02.

ND Highway Patrol HB 1298 study final report (2026)
Valley News Live - 119 mph reckless arrest (2026)

ND.notes: Fee formula reconstructed from bill text (struck/new text merged) and checked against Highway Patrol 2026 examples and a news-reported $215 for 39 over on I-29. Official codified NDCC not read. 2027 session will consider higher fines/points (HP study). HP report mentions 30+ over as reckless, not confirmed in statute text.

OH.name: Ohio

default_limits.basis: ORC 4511.21(B): 25 in municipalities (35 on state routes outside business districts), 55 outside municipalities, 70 rural freeways (65 urban, 55 congested), 20 school zones, 15 alleys

fine.notes: Minor misdemeanor, max $150. Each court sets a waiver schedule. Example (Erie Co.): $3-$6/mph over, $150 at 30+ over, plus costs.

court_costs.notes: Varies by court. Sampled: Erie Co. $100, Cleveland Muni $125, Mentor Muni $152.

points.notes: ORC 4510.036: on limits of 55+, 0 pts up to 10 over, 2 pts 11-29. Under 55: 0 pts up to 5 over. 30+ over = 4 pts. 12 pts in 2 yrs = suspension.

zones.work_zone: Fine doubled when construction-zone sign posted (ORC 4511.21(P)(3)).
zones.school_zone: 20 mph at school times; over 35 is a 4th-degree misdemeanor.

court.reason: 4 points; top waiver bracket in many courts.

arrest.offense: 4th-degree misdemeanor speeding (location-specific, see notes)

trucks.notes: Not researched.

OH.notes: No statewide mph-over criminal threshold. Speeding is an M4 (30 days/$250) if over 35 in a municipal business district or school zone, or over 50 elsewhere in a municipality; also M4/M3 for 3rd/4th speeding conviction in a year. Residential 25 applies only inside municipalities; township roads default 55. HB 111 (extra fine at 30+ over) is only introduced.

OK.name: Oklahoma

default_limits.basis: 47 O.S. § 11-801 (not read directly). Only secondary sources found: 55 most county roads, 35 state parks, 25 most school zones. Other defaults unverified.

fine.notes: Base fines from a secondary source, unverified against statute. Court costs and assessments add much more.

court_costs.notes: Varies by court. Example: Lawton municipal court total (fine+costs) $195 for 1–10 over, $295 for 31+ (2017 schedule).

points.notes: Point values from secondary sources that disagree (1–10 over: 0 or 1). 10+ points in 5 years = suspension (OAC 670:15-15-6).

zones.work_zone: Higher fines (secondary sources say doubled); amount unverified.
zones.school_zone: Higher fines (secondary sources say doubled); amount unverified.

court.reason: No statewide mandatory-court threshold found.

arrest.offense: Reckless driving (misdemeanor)

trucks.notes: Not researched; unknown.

OK.notes: Official statutes (OSCN, oklegislature.gov) were unreachable this session. Reckless driving: 5–90 days and $100–$500 per secondary source; no mph threshold found. Needs a verification pass before release.

OR.name: Oregon

default_limits.basis: ORS 811.111(1): 65 interstates; 55 elsewhere; 25 residence district (non-arterial) and public parks; 20 business district; 15 alleys/narrow residential roads; 20 school zones when flashing or 7am-5pm school days. Some designated highways 60-70 by sign.

fine.notes: Presumptive fines (ORS 153.019, court schedule SOF-24) for limits under 65. On 65+ mph roads classes shift up: 1-10 over $165, 11-20 $265, 21+ $440. 100+ mph: $1,150. Max by class: D $250, C $500, B $1,000, A $2,000.

court_costs.notes: No separate court cost on the presumptive fine. Jefferson and Multnomah counties add a $5 surcharge. Restitution/costs may be added if contested.

points.notes: No points system. Adults (18+): 3 convictions/preventable crashes in 24 months = 30-day night restriction; 5 = 30-day suspension (OAR 735-072-0027).

zones.work_zone: Higher presumptive fines in posted highway work zones and safety corridors: D $225, C $325, B $525, A $875 (ORS 153.020).
zones.school_zone: 20 mph when lights flash or 7am-5pm school days; same higher zone fines as work zones (ORS 153.020).

court.reason: Top Class A fine ($440; 21+ over on 65+ roads). 100+ mph: $1,150 fine and mandatory 30-90 day license suspension.

arrest.offense: Reckless driving (Class A misdemeanor) - no speed number; requires reckless endangerment of people or property
arrest.license: Speeding alone is never criminal, even 100+ mph (violation with 30-90 day suspension). Reckless-driving suspension not verified.

trucks.notes: Trucks over 10,000 lb GVWR, truck tractors over 8,000 lb, school/worker/church buses: 55 on any highway unless posted otherwise (ORS 811.111(1)(b)). Designated interstate/highway segments post 60-65 for trucks vs 65-70 for cars.

sources.title: Oregon Judicial Dept. Schedule of Fines on Violations SOF-24
SB 615 (2023) impact statement - reckless driving penalties

OR.notes: Speed limits and 100 mph rule read via public.law (2023 ORS + 2024 changes); fines from official 2025 ORS and SOF-24 (eff. 9/1/2024). Reckless driving max from SB 615 summary, not the statute itself. A court may add up to 30 days suspension for 31+ over with a prior within 12 months.

PA.name: Pennsylvania

default_limits.basis: 75 Pa.C.S. § 3362(a): 35 in urban districts; 25 in residence districts on local, non-numbered roads; 55 elsewhere; 65/70 on freeways only where posted. Residential 25 assumes a residence district; in other urban districts the default is 35.

fine.notes: $35 + $2 per mph beyond 5 over (§ 3362(c)); e.g. 10 over = $45. On 65+ mph limits base is $42.50 (10 over = $52.50). No cap. Summary offense.

court_costs.notes: Court costs plus surcharges (EMS $10, JCP $10, MCARE, etc. per 2014 PennDOT-funded card) added; current total not found in an official source. Often exceeds the fine.

points.notes: 31+ over: 5 pts + PennDOT hearing, possible 15-day suspension and/or driving exam. 11 pts = automatic suspension. Under-18: 26+ over = 90-day suspension.

zones.work_zone: Fines doubled in active work zones with workers present (e.g. $45 becomes $90). 15-day suspension for 11+ over reported by secondary source; not verified.
zones.school_zone: Same $35 + $2/mph formula; 11+ over: up to $500 fine and 3 pts (2014 PennDOT-funded card).

court.reason: 31+ over: PennDOT departmental hearing; possible 15-day suspension or special driving exam.

arrest.offense: None by speed. Speeding and reckless driving (§ 3736) are both summary offenses.
arrest.citation: 75 Pa.C.S. § 3736 (reckless driving: summary offense, $200 fine, no speed number)

trucks.notes: § 3362(a) as read sets no truck-specific default; PennDOT may post truck limits on specific roads.

sources.title: PennDOT Point System Fact Sheet (Nov 2013, via Delaware County courts)

PA.notes: No criminal speeding threshold: PA speeding and reckless driving are summary offenses (fine only, no speed number). Statute text read shows last amendment 2014; points fact sheet dated 2013. Court costs not verified.

RI.name: Rhode Island

default_limits.basis: R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-14-2 prima facie limits: 25 in business or residence districts; 50 daytime / 45 nighttime elsewhere (night = 30 min after sunset to 30 min before sunrise). Higher limits (e.g. interstates) apply only where posted after the state alters them. Non-residential values shown are daytime.

fine.notes: 1-10 over: $95. 11+ over: $10 per mph over, $205 minimum (app shows $95 + $10/mph, which equals $205 at 11 over; statute wording is ambiguous). Repeat offenses within 12 months cost more per mph (§ 31-41.1-4).

court_costs.notes: $1 EMS fee + $3.25 tech surcharge per summons. Another $35 court cost if you're found guilty at a hearing (RI Traffic Tribunal FAQ).

points.notes: No DMV point system (secondary source). Instead a judge may suspend your license: up to 30 days for 1-10 over, up to 60 days for 11+ over (§ 31-41.1-4(b)).

zones.work_zone: Not verified.
zones.school_zone: 20 mph within 300 ft of school entrances on school days in daytime, where signs are posted (§ 31-14-2). Higher school-zone fines were proposed in 2026 (S 2718/H 8481) but not verified as enacted.

court.reason: Mandatory per-mph fine ($205+), and a judge may suspend your license up to 60 days.

arrest.offense: Reckless driving (misdemeanor). No speed number in the statute; it depends on the conduct.
arrest.license: DMV may suspend up to 1 year (secondary source)

trucks.notes: Not verified.

sources.title: RI Traffic Tribunal FAQ (costs and fees)
RI Traffic Tribunal Know Your Rights
RI ACLU on 2026 driving penalty bills

RI.notes: Defaults and the fine schedule come from the statute. Reckless-driving penalties ($500, 1 yr) are from a secondary source; the statute text wasn't readable. 2026 S 2493 would make reckless driving at 25+ mph a felony (up to 5 yrs, $1,000-$5,000), but § 31-27-4 was last amended in 2007, so it hasn't been enacted.

SC.name: South Carolina

default_limits.basis: S.C. Code 56-5-1520: 30 urban district; 40 unpaved roads; 55 other locations. 70 interstate / 60 multilane divided primary only where posted.

fine.notes: Statute sets ranges; values shown are maximums: $15-25, $25-50, $50-75, $75-200 (56-5-1520(G)). Exactly 15 and exactly 25 over fall in gaps in the text.

court_costs.notes: Assessments roughly double the fine. Example (Clemson municipal court): totals $76.75 / $128.75 / $180.50 / $440 by bracket.

points.notes: 56-1-720. Reckless driving = 6 points.

zones.work_zone: Not verified.
zones.school_zone: Not verified.

court.reason: 25+ over: 6 points and fine up to $200.

arrest.offense: Speeding more than 25 over (misdemeanor, jail possible)
arrest.license: 6 points

trucks.notes: Only manufactured/mobile homes in transport: 10 below posted, max 55.

SC.notes: Statute text read via bills quoting current law (code site not reachable). All SC speeding is a misdemeanor. Reckless driving (56-5-2920) has no speed number; penalty not verified. Court-cost example dates to 2008 guidance.

SD.name: South Dakota

default_limits.basis: SDCL 32-25-4 (80 interstates), 32-25-1.1 (65 all other streets/highways unless posted), 32-25-12 (25 unposted urban areas), 32-25-9.2 (55 township roads). Divided 4-lane rural highways may be posted 70 (32-25-7.1). OSM mapping approximate.

fine.notes: Statewide UJS fine schedule FY2027 (eff. 7/1/2026), same for interstate, highways and other roads. With $78.50 costs: $97.50 to $232.50. Speeding is a Class 2 misdemeanor (SDCL 32-25-7); statutory max not verified. City ordinance tickets may differ.

court_costs.notes: Fixed statewide: $50 liquidated costs, $23.50 court automation, $5 victim comp.

points.notes: Speeding carries 0 points. Reckless driving 8 pts. Suspension at 15 pts/12 mo or 22 pts/24 mo.

zones.work_zone: Construction zone fine doubles: $38 (1-5 over) to $308 (26+); totals $116.50-$386.50.

court.reason: Top bracket: fine jumps from $99 to $154 ($232.50 total). Still payable; no mandatory appearance on the schedule.

arrest.offense: Reckless driving (Class 1 misdemeanor) - no speed number; requires driving that endangers people or property
arrest.license: 8 points; no mandatory revocation on 1st (30-day revocation on 2nd within 1 year)

trucks.notes: Transportation Commission may set lower limits by rule for vehicles over 10,000 lb (32-25-6). Rule values not verified.

SD.notes: Fines, costs, limits high confidence. Every speeding ticket is technically a Class 2 misdemeanor (SDCL 32-25-4, 32-25-7; max penalty not verified from source), but it is paid off the schedule. Reckless penalty from secondary site (statute text not read). 2025 HB 1175 proposed 'aggravated careless driving' at 20+ over (Class 1); not found in code, enactment unconfirmed.

TN.name: Tennessee

default_limits.basis: Tenn. Code 55-8-152 per TN Governor's Highway Safety Office: statutory max 70 on 4+ lane controlled-access interstate/state highways, 65 other public roads. Cities may set lower limits (max 55) and often set 30 by ordinance (55-8-153). No statewide residential default found.

fine.notes: Speeding is a Class C misdemeanor: fine up to $50 (40-35-111(e)(3)). Totals with costs vary by county; range shown is Montgomery Co. General Sessions 2026 schedule (fine + costs).

court_costs.notes: Varies by county and court; included in county totals above (Montgomery Co. ~$120-232 beyond the $50 fine). No statewide figure found.

points.notes: Tenn. Comp. R. & Regs. 1340-01-04-.03. Reckless = 6 pts. 12 pts in 12 months = suspension (secondary source).

zones.work_zone: Higher fines (reportedly $250+) in work zones under 55-8-152 (secondary source; not verified).
zones.school_zone: Cities/counties may set school-zone limits, not below 15 mph (55-8-152); penalty not verified.

court.reason: No statewide mandatory-court speed threshold found.

arrest.offense: Any speeding is a Class C misdemeanor; reckless driving (Class B) has no speed number
arrest.license: Points only; reckless driving 6 pts

trucks.notes: No truck-specific limit found in sources read; not exhaustively checked.

TN.notes: Statute text of 55-8-152 not read (official code is on Lexis); limits from state GHSO summary. Every speeding charge is criminal (Class C) but normally cite-and-release; no special criminal speed tier. Montgomery schedule's per-mph columns were unlabeled in extraction, so only the total range is used. City courts limited to $50 fines (16-18-302). 2023 bill to raise interstate limit to 75 did not pass.

TX.name: Texas

default_limits.basis: Tex. Transp. Code § 545.352(b): 30 urban district (15 alley); outside urban district 70 on US/state-numbered highways incl. FM/RM roads, 60 on other highways. OSM mapping assumes numbered = secondary and above; inside a city, unposted streets are 30.

fine.notes: Each court sets its own fine within the $1–$200 statutory range (§ 542.401). Range shown is the statutory range, not observed averages.

court_costs.notes: Mandatory on conviction: $62 state + $14 local consolidated court costs, $50 state traffic fine (§ 542.4031), $3 local traffic fine. Extra fees possible (e.g. $15 time-payment fee).

points.notes: No points since the Driver Responsibility Program was repealed 9/1/2019. Habitual violator suspension: 4+ moving convictions in 12 months or 7+ in 24 months (§ 521.292).

zones.work_zone: Min and max fine doubled when workers present and the limit is posted (§ 542.404).
zones.school_zone: No statewide fine doubling found; school-zone limits are set and posted locally.

court.reason: Not eligible for driving-safety-course dismissal at 25+ over or 95+ mph (CCP art. 45A.352(a)(5)).

arrest.offense: Reckless driving (misdemeanor)

trucks.notes: Separate truck and nighttime limits were repealed effective 9/1/2011 (HB 1353); school buses have lower limits.

Tex. Code Crim. Proc. art. 45A.352 (driving safety course)

TX.notes: Speeding itself is a fine-only Class C misdemeanor; officers must issue a citation, not arrest, if the driver signs a promise to appear (§ 543.004). Reckless driving has no mph threshold. 2025 SB 2799 (felony reckless if injury) passed the Senate; final enactment not verified. Statute text read via public.law/Justia mirrors because the official statutes site was blocked.

UT.name: Utah

default_limits.basis: Utah Code § 41-6a-601(2): 25 in urban districts, 55 elsewhere, 20 in reduced-speed school zones. Posted limits up to 65 (75 on freeways, higher if UDOT study) under § 41-6a-602.

fine.notes: Suggested fines (Judicial Council schedule, as copied in a county court's 2023 bail schedule). 31+ over: $480 + $10 per mph beyond 31. At 100+ mph court must impose at least 150% of scheduled fine. Infraction max $750.

court_costs.notes: Security surcharge $60 (justice court) / $53 (district) is already included in the suggested fines above. +$50 if not paid within 14 days (county schedule).

points.notes: Reckless = 80 pts. 200 pts in 3 yrs (70 if age 20 or under) can mean suspension. Points drop off after 3 yrs.

zones.work_zone: Higher construction-zone fines: $180 (1-10 over) up to $680 (26-30 over) on county schedule.
zones.school_zone: 20 mph when posted. School-zone speeding is a class C misdemeanor (§ 41-6a-604) with higher fines; possible crossing-guard service.

court.reason: At 100+ mph the court must impose at least 150% of the scheduled fine (§ 41-6a-601(4)).

arrest.offense: Reckless driving (class B misdemeanor); 105+ mph is reckless by law
arrest.license: 80 points; counts toward 200-point suspension

trucks.notes: No separate statutory truck limit found; UDOT may post limits by vehicle type (§ 41-6a-602(2)).

DrivingLaws.org UT speeding (secondary, confirms fine brackets)

UT.notes: Ordinary speeding is an infraction (§ 41-6a-601(4)), not a class C misdemeanor; school-zone speeding is class C. Only 105+ mph is reckless by speed; no mph-over threshold (a 2022 bill proposing 100 mph/25 over was enacted as 105 only). Fines from a 2023 county copy of the state schedule; 2026 rows unverified. Reckless also gets a 90% criminal surcharge.

VT.name: Vermont

default_limits.basis: 23 V.S.A. § 1081(b): 50 mph unless another limit is set. 65 on limited-access highways is set by rule (CVR 14-053-004 art. 1.1, under § 1004). There's no statutory residential default; towns post 25-50 (§ 1007).

fine.notes: Judicial Bureau waiver: mph over x $5/$6/$8/$12 by bracket, plus surcharges (see court costs). Totals: 1 over $53, 10 over $105, 20 over $185, 30 over $323, 31 over $475.

court_costs.notes: Add $47 plus 15% of the fine (rounded up) to the base fine (Judicial Bureau waiver schedule). If you lose a hearing, the judge may also add a court fee.

points.notes: 23 V.S.A. § 2502 and Judicial Bureau speed chart. Collected points can lead to a DMV suspension; the threshold wasn't verified.

zones.work_zone: Double the per-mph waiver rate ($10/$12/$16/$24). Chart lists a work zone max of $2,347.
zones.school_zone: Double the per-mph waiver rate ($10/$12/$16/$24) where posted.

court.reason: Criminal excessive speed (30+ over AND 60+ mph) goes to criminal court, not the Judicial Bureau.

arrest.offense: Excessive speed (criminal): 60+ mph AND 30+ over the limit
arrest.license: 8 points

trucks.notes: No separate truck limit found. Commercial vehicles pay higher per-mph waiver rates.

VT.notes: § 1097 requires BOTH 60+ mph AND 30+ over, so use and_min_speed (60) as an AND condition, not OR. The schedule's chart totals match the formula exactly. Negligent operation (§ 1091) can also be charged at any speed. The suspension point threshold wasn't verified.

VA.name: Virginia

default_limits.basis: Va. Code § 46.2-870 (55 unless posted; up to 70 only where posted after study), § 46.2-874 (25 in business/residence districts), § 46.2-873.1 (35 on unpaved roads)

fine.notes: $6/mph over on prepayable schedule (§ 46.2-878.3). +$100 if 80-85 on a 65 road. $7/mph school/work zone, $8/mph posted residence district. Infraction max = Class 4 misd. fine ($250).

court_costs.notes: Fixed $51 district court fee per traffic infraction (§ 16.1-69.48:1).

points.notes: DMV demerit points. Reckless by speed (20+ over or >85) = 6 pts, stays 11 yrs.

zones.work_zone: Up to $500 fine when workers present (§ 46.2-878.1); $7/mph on prepay schedule.
zones.school_zone: 25 mph when flashing/posted; up to $250 fine (§ 46.2-873); $7/mph on prepay schedule.

court.reason: Becomes reckless driving: not prepayable, must go to court.

arrest.offense: Reckless driving by speed (Class 1 misdemeanor)
arrest.license: Court may suspend 10 days to 6 months (§ 46.2-392); over 100 mph: suspension or Intelligent Speed Assistance required (§ 46.2-507, eff. 7/1/2026)

trucks.notes: Trucks, tractor trucks, property-carrying combos, and vehicles towing house trailers: 45 mph on highways other than interstates, 4+ lane roads and primary highways (§ 46.2-870).

VA.notes: Reckless = 20+ over OR over 85 mph regardless of limit. Residence-district 25 applies only in legally defined districts; rural local roads default to 55. Unpaved roads default 35. Some localities' prepay totals add local fees beyond $51.

WA.name: Washington

default_limits.basis: RCW 46.61.400(2): 25 city/town streets, 50 county roads, 60 state highways. Defaults depend on jurisdiction, not road type; OSM mapping is approximate (a county residential road defaults to 50, a state-route tertiary to 60). Max posted allowed 75 (RCW 46.61.410).

fine.notes: Base penalties from IRLJ 6.2 for limits over 40 mph. Limits 40 or less: 1-5 $43, 6-10 $48, 11-15 $63, 16-20 $83, 21-25 $108, 26-30 $133, 31-35 $158, 36+ $188. Assessments roughly double the ticket (see court_costs).

court_costs.notes: Fixed $49 add-ons (RCW 46.63.110: $5+$10+$10+$24) plus PSEA of 105% of base (RCW 3.62.090: 70% + half of that). Est. total = base x 2.05 + $49 (e.g. 1-5 over in 60 zone ~ $117). Not confirmed against an official total table.

points.notes: No points system. 3 moving-violation stops in 12 months or 4 in 24 months = 60-day suspension, then 1-year probation (DOL).

zones.work_zone: Speeding penalty doubled in roadway construction zones; cannot be waived or reduced (RCW 46.61.527). Endangering workers is a gross misdemeanor with 60-day suspension.
zones.school_zone: 20 mph when posted; penalty doubled and cannot be waived, reduced or suspended (RCW 46.61.440).

court.reason: All speeding is a civil traffic infraction; no speed triggers a mandatory court appearance or automatic suspension.

arrest.offense: Reckless driving (gross misdemeanor) - no speed number; requires willful or wanton disregard for safety
arrest.license: suspension of at least 30 days

trucks.notes: Vehicles over 10,000 lb GVW and all vehicle combinations (towing), except auto stages: max 60 mph, even where cars may go 70 (RCW 46.61.410(2)-(3)).

sources.title: WA DOL - accumulation of traffic tickets
SDOT blog - work zone double fines (secondary)
ESB 5890 House bill report 2026 (reckless driving background)

WA.notes: No criminal speed threshold: SB 5238 (2025) and ESB 5890 (2026, 30+ over = reckless) both died. Excess speed is prima facie evidence of recklessness (RCW 46.61.465), so arrest is possible at officer discretion. From 2029, reckless convictions add a speed-limiter probation (2025 c 228). Work-zone statute text read via secondary source only.

WV.name: West Virginia

default_limits.basis: W. Va. Code § 17C-6-1(b): 25 business/residence district, 15 school zone (recess/arrival/dismissal), 55 open country. Interstates/controlled-access set by posting (min 55), no fixed default.

fine.notes: Misdemeanor; 1st offense fine up to $100 (2nd in 1 yr $200, 3rd in 2 yrs $500). Interstate 10 or less over: max $5 + costs, not reported to DMV.

points.notes: 10 or less over = no points (except CDL). Reckless = 6 pts (W. Va. CSR § 91-5-7).

court.reason: Points jump to 5-6; 15+ over makes 3rd offense jailable.

arrest.offense: Reckless driving (no speed threshold; 'willful or wanton disregard')
arrest.license: 6 points

trucks.notes: No general truck limit; coal haulers on coal road system face tripled fines (§ 17C-6-1(h)).

WV.notes: No speed-based criminal threshold. All speeding is technically a misdemeanor but fine-only for 1st offense. HB 4829 (2026) would make 30+ over reckless; it stalled in committee. Reckless 1st offense: 5-90 days jail and/or $25-$500. Court costs unknown.

fine.notes: Civil forfeiture $30-$300 (freeway/expressway $50-$300), plus fees. Deposit set by statewide schedule; per-mph brackets not verified.

WY.name: Wyoming

default_limits.basis: W.S. 31-5-301(b): 30 urban/residence districts, 75 interstates (80 where designated), 70 non-interstate state highways, 65 other paved roads, 55 unpaved roads, 20 school zones when signed. OSM mapping approximate; unpaved unclassified/track roads = 55.

fine.notes: Uniform Bail & Forfeiture Schedule (eff. 7/1/2026), interstates/highways/other roads. Fine shown excludes $75 fees. 1-5 over: $5/mph, no fees. 6-10: $30+$2/mph over 5. 11-20: $45+$5/mph over 10. 21+: $95+$5/mph over 20 (30+ over row computes -$5 + $5/mph = $95 + $5/mph over 20). Urban districts: 1-5 $65+$2/mph (no fees); 6-10 $40+$7/mph over 5; 11-20 $95+$7/mph over 10; 21+ $195+$7/mph over 20 (+fees). Statutory max not verified.

court_costs.notes: Fixed statewide, added only at 6+ over: $20 court costs, $40 court automation, $10 civil legal services, $5 officer training. None at 1-5 over.

points.notes: No points. WYDOT: 4th moving violation in 12 months = 90-day suspension; each further one adds 90 days. Up to 80 mph in 65-75 zones, or under 6 over elsewhere, is not put on the driving record (31-5-301(d); not school/work zone or CDL).

zones.work_zone: Construction zones use the urban-district fine table (1-5 over $67-75; 6+ over $40+$7/mph plus fees).
zones.school_zone: 20 mph when signed. 1-5 over $50+$2/mph; 6-10 $95+$10/mph over 5 plus fees (e.g. 6 over $180 total); 11+ $200+$10/mph over 10 plus fees (e.g. 11 over $285).

court.reason: At 6+ over the $75 fees kick in (total jumps from $25 to $107+ on highways) and the ticket can go on the driving record. All speeding is bond-forfeitable (pay without court) if the officer marks it so.

arrest.offense: Reckless driving (misdemeanor) - no speed number; requires willful or wanton disregard for safety
arrest.license: 90-day suspension on 1st conviction (WYDOT)

trucks.notes: No separate truck limits found in 31-5-301. Heavy vehicles pay +$295 on 6+ over tickets (31-5-1201(g)).
